findings.finding: Redaction is inert in production: grep -rn register_sensitive backend/src/ finds only a docstring and the definition — zero call sites. With nothing registered, scrub_text returns every PAN, Aadhaar, salary-document name, absolute path and connection string unchanged. Observed live: GET /applicants/ABCDE1234F/123412341234 logged "message": "GET /applicants/ABCDE1234F/123412341234 -> 404", and X-Request-ID: ABCDE1234F-123412341234 logged "request_id": "ABCDE1234F-123412341234" — raw PAN and raw Aadhaar in the log sink, on the only endpoints that exist. AC1 passes because its fixture registers the values itself. ba457bf added the call sites to the story text of E1-S1 and E4-S1; no code carries one.
findings.suggestion: Either land a call site now, or add a request-time assertion so the criterion cannot pass while the substrate is inert.

findings.finding: f5a5ace's fix is structurally inert. sanitise_context now routes ints and keys through scrub_text, but scrub_text is registration-driven, so with nothing registered an AppError context egressed on the wire: "aadhaar_int": 123412341234 (12-digit Aadhaar, whole, as an int), "pan-ABCDE1234F": "ok" (PAN in the key, verbatim), "path": "C:/Users/rosuo/secret/payslip.pdf" (absolute path). The connection string, the nested mapping and the 300-char value WERE dropped — those use pattern and length rules rather than registration. Round-2 SEC-003 is still open.
findings.suggestion: Add pattern-based rules for Aadhaar/PAN shapes and for absolute paths, independent of registration.

findings.finding: Redaction bypass by formatting, confirmed far past the 5-dash case. With ABCDE1234F / 123412341234 / salary_slip_march.pdf all registered: exact, spaced and dashed Aadhaar redact; dotted, underscored, slashed, NBSP-, soft-hyphen-, zero-width- and fullwidth-separated forms all egress unchanged.
findings.suggestion: Normalize (NFKC + strip separators and format-control characters) then match.

findings.finding: `method` is an unbounded label dimension in the app's own code. Under --http h11 one keep-alive connection minted 22,003 method label values, 330,064 exposition lines and a 25.3 MB /metrics payload, retained for the process lifetime. httptools bounds it today by accident of llhttp's method enum, not by anything the application does.
findings.suggestion: Bound `method` to a known-method allow-list beside route_label, collapsing anything else to one <unknown> bucket. Three lines.

findings.finding: _escape_label is not a general escaper. Measured: LF, quote and backslash are escaped; CR, TAB, NUL, BEL, ESC and DEL all survive as raw control characters. AC2's 'no raw control character' holds in the exposition today only because no attacker-controlled string can currently reach a label. The first story that labels a series with user-derived text breaks AC2 with no test failing.
findings.suggestion: Escape or reject the whole C0/C1 range, not three characters.

findings.finding: /openapi.json, /docs and /redoc are real routed endpoints but label as route="<unmatched>" — 61 successful 200s landed in the same bucket as 20 garbage-path 404s. route_label() reads scope['route'].path, which FastAPI's APIRoute populates and the plain Starlette routes FastAPI mounts for its docs do not.
findings.suggestion: Fall back to the matched Starlette route's path when scope['route'] is absent but the status is not 404.

findings.finding: AC1's Given names a schedule this story never builds. The criterion is unsatisfiable end-to-end inside group A and its test is a Money-level surrogate that tests/architecture/test_no_float_money.py:8 admits in its own docstring.
findings.suggestion: Re-point the AC at Money, or move it to E9-S3.

findings.finding: Money.multiply lets a bare decimal.Overflow escape — round 2's dispute resolved by execution. Money(Decimal('1.00')).multiply(Decimal('1e1000000')) raises decimal.Overflow, NOT the documented InvalidMoneyAmountError, in 0.000 s (round 2's 9,708 ms reading was noise; the escape is instantaneous and real). 1e999999 is caught correctly; the cliff is at Emax. Overflow is an ArithmeticError, so the API boundary maps it to a generic 500 instead of a typed 4xx.
findings.suggestion: Catch decimal.DecimalException (or at least Overflow and Underflow) in multiply and _quantize.

findings.finding: X-Request-ID is unvalidated and unbounded — worse than round 2 recorded. A 1 MB header value was accepted, echoed on the response, and produced a single log line of 1,048,722 bytes. One request writes 1 MB to the log sink; the amplification is uncapped.
findings.suggestion: Cap the inbound id (e.g. 128 chars, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) and regenerate on violation.

findings.finding: Host-header-reflected open redirect, still open. GET /health/ with Host: evil.example -> 307 with location: http://evil.example/health; Host: attacker.test:8080 -> location: http://attacker.test:8080/health.
findings.suggestion: Add TrustedHostMiddleware, or build redirects relative.

findings.finding: No security response headers on /health: Strict-Transport-Security, Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Cache-Control all absent. Server: uvicorn disclosed.

/docs (200, 1015 B), /redoc (200, 897 B), /openapi.json (200, 738 B) and /metrics (200, 13,310 B) are all unauthenticated. The /metrics deferral is documented in E15-S4 Scope Out and I judge it ACCEPTABLE — auth genuinely needs the api-contracts.md amendment and the E1-S1 auth layer, and a bare RED counter set on a pre-production build is low-value to an attacker. F-2 raises the stakes: an unauthenticated 25.3 MB response is amplification, so the deferral should be revisited the moment F-2 is fixed rather than at E1-S1. The interactive docs surfaces carry no such documented deferral.
HEAD /health -> 405, still open. RFC 9110 9.3.2: a server supporting GET on a resource ought to support HEAD. Container and load-balancer probes commonly use HEAD.
_STATUS_ERROR_NAMES has no entry for 405, so the envelope reads "error":"HTTPError" rather than a named MethodNotAllowed.

The 500's traceback is logged with absolute filesystem paths, the database connection string and the SQL text intact. It stays out of the response body, correctly, but the log sink receives it unscrubbed — a direct consequence of F-1.
